Our results reveal that the external field has a distinct impact on all even cumulants except the second-order one, causing them to become zero at h=0, while the third and fourth-order cumulants exhibit symmetry under this condition. Notably, the behavior of the second-order cumulant remains unchanged, displaying no zero-value point at h=0. Furthermore, we have derived an explicit formula for the magnetic susceptibility at the critical temperature, which takes the form 1/(k_B T) * (1 + 2h^2).

Researchers study the properties of certain 6-dimensional tensors that are related to matrix product operators used in physics studies of 2-dimensional situations without obvious order. By analyzing a specific algebraic structure, researchers are able to express these tensors in a more manageable form and confirm that they are consistent with expectations set by physics theories. The study also reveals that a specific property of one of these tensors aligns with patterns observed in situations with symmetry and fractal patterns. The findings are verified through numerical simulations and also occur in scenarios where interactions between particles follow random patterns. The study shows that the algebraic structure is sufficient to produce the same results as more complex physics simulations. The research may lead to a better understanding of the relationship between the algebraic structure and the properties of the tensors, and as a result, the study is extending the framework to include more complex algebraic structures and 4-dimensional tensors related to entanglement and anyons.

Hamiltonian Neural Networks have been shown to be effective in modeling dynamical systems, and our analysis demonstrates that they can be viewed as meta-learners that generalize system behavior from training data. We then take this concept a step further and experimentally prove that HNNs perform better than LSTM-based meta-learners in tasks involving the MNIST dataset, and that this advantage diminishes as the training data becomes more representative of the target system. Additionally, our findings support the idea that HNNs can be seen as a type of dynamical system that incorporates a learning component, and we believe this discovery has the potential to expand the applications of HNNs in the future.

In the context of a decentralized system, we suggest a multi-agent network that utilizes a novel score metric called trust value for evaluating the reliability of machine learning models. In this setup, multiple agents contribute their towards achieving a common goal by utilizing their own individual learning algorithms, and the results show that using the proposed trust value, models achieve a 10% higher accuracy and a 50% higher trust score when compared to models that don't use trust value, across various datasets.

Airports face significant challenges in preventing prohibited items from entering their facilities. To address this issue, it is crucial to develop advanced technologies for detecting concealed items. The primary obstacle in doing so is the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing collections of prohibited items images are limited in scope, focusing on specific categories such as firearms, knives, and explosives. Moreover, they lack diversity in terms of prohibited items, with only a handful of rare items represented. Moreover, current approaches to prohibited items detection suffer from low precision and recall rates due to over-reliance on deep learning methods that prioritize easy targets over harder ones. To address these limitations, we introduce HiXray, the largest X-ray-scanned dataset of prohibited items to date, featuring 1,000 unique items from 80 distinct categories. To further assess the performance of detection algorithms, we created HiXray-12k, an expanded version of the dataset with 12,000 images. To evaluate state-of-the-art methods on this challenging task, we present HiXray-score, a comprehensive evaluation metric that quantifies the accuracy of detecting both the presence and type of prohibited items. Notably, we observed that existing deep learning-based approaches fail to excel in prohibited items detection, with a mean average precision of just 0.453. To improve performance, we introduced an auxiliary classification task that prioritizes difficult items, leading to a significant boost in precision to 0.734 + 0.034, outperforming the baseline model

A new polynomial invariant called $J_n^T$ has been introduced and its properties are being explored. Initially, it was believed to produce invariants for torus links. However, recent discoveries indicate that $J_n^T$ actually produces invariants for a broader class of links known as $(p,q,r)s\cdot L(1,1)$ links. This paper will delimit the scope of $J_n^T$ even further by determining that it only applies to links of the form $(p,q)s\cdot L(1,1)$, and will also establish a connection to another polynomial called $Q_n$, leading to the ability to calculate the $J_n^T$ values for these specific links.

Deep learning models have achieved high accuracy on various natural language processing tasks, but they can be vulnerable to data corruption and typically require large, carefully labeled datasets. Data augmentation methods have been shown to enhance performance and model robustness by generating new labeled data from existing sets, but their effectiveness depends on the method used. In this study, three simple data augmentation techniques are examined: word dropping, syllable substitution, and part-of-speech guided word replacement. The experiments demonstrate that these methods improve the performance of a deep learning model on the TIMIT speech recognition task and the UCI text classification tasks, leading to a 4.2% absolute reduction in error rate on TIMIT and a 1.7% absolute improvement in F-score on average.

This work extends the complex representation of the Gamma function to a broader class of functions, including the Beta and Gamma beta functions, hypergeometric functions like $_2F_1$, and confluent hypergeometric functions like $M$. By utilizing a Hankel path in the complex plane, these representations become possible, leading to novel analytic continuations, and enabling the evaluation of these functions at negative numbers.

The LHCb Collaboration recorded a unique dataset at 13 TeV center-of-mass energy, allowing for the measurement of top quark production in differential cross-sections. Contrary to conventional approaches, this study utilized final-state hadronic systems with significant energy, often discarded in other analyses, and employed an advanced method of determining the jet's mass. The analysis focused on the $b$-jet's properties, such as whether it was produced alone or in conjunction with other jets, as well as the jet's energy within certain ranges. The findings were compared to theoretical predictions from perturbative quantum chromodynamics, revealing a significant discrepancy, particularly noticeable when considering the $b$-jet's own energy rather than the total energy across all jets.

Our research introduces an innovative approach to evaluating SQL queries without access to complete database data. Distinguishing our method from existing solutions, our framework achieves high accuracy in query evaluation, attaining a 99% success rate in testing scenarios. Unlike previous techniques that heavily rely on database contents, our approach utilizes a limited number of queries with known results to achieve this level of precision. In contrast, existing solutions without database contents typically achieve a 50-60% accuracy rate. Building upon the work of [1], we enhance the query evaluation process by introducing an iterative optimization technique that refines our predictions and eliminates unnecessary variables. The performance of this algorithm is demonstrated through experimental results presented in the paper.

When teaching a student's private data using differentially private methods like the Laplace mechanism, it's challenging to estimate the probability of a specific query outcome because of the complex connections between students' graded performances in a graph structure. Consequently, accurately calculating the probability of a specific outcome, such as determining if John scored higher than Mary, becomes extremely difficult. In this study, we demonstrate that indeed no accurate method exists to calculate these probabilities and present a new approach that works for discrete queries in graph structures. This approach involves assigning a unique identifier to each data point and generating a new set of fake data points with a specific structure, allowing for accurate computation of privacy loss. We show that this approach is efficient and can be used in conjunction with other differentially private methods, such as the Laplace mechanism. Notably, our method provides an exact solution, in contrast to previous methods that offered approximations.

The Euclid mission, set to launch in 2022, will significantly contribute to various astronomical disciplines through its extensive data collection. As part of a comprehensive assessment, this study examines potential advancements in astronomical research powered by Euclid's data. Ten renowned experts in specific fields, such as exoplanets, stellar astrospheres, stellar activity, stellar oscillations, stellar clusters, stellar rotation, stellar properties, stellar magnetic fields, stellar mass accretion, and stellar extinction, provided valuable insights in a series of workshops. Their input highlights the potential of Euclid to make groundbreaking discoveries and address key research questions in their respective fields.

Evaluating the safety of fully automated lane-keeping systems relies heavily on realistic testing, but conducting a large number of human-driven tests is costly and time-consuming. To accelerate the evaluation process, we suggest generating complex road networks that could potentially cause these systems to fail. By developing a procedure to create multiple types of hazardous scenarios through a combination of route planning and map editing, we aim to demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in identifying vulnerabilities in automated lane-keeping systems via a case study involving one such system.

The success of music streaming platforms relies heavily on recommending personalized playlists to users. To achieve this, audio content analysis is a crucial step that can offer valuable insights into the characteristics of music content. Recently, using deep learning models such as convolutional neural networks (CNN) has become a popular approach for audio-based applications. However, applying traditional deep learning models to real-world music datasets is complicated due to the large size of the data and the need for labeled samples. In the music industry, access to such labeled data is often restricted. In this paper, we demonstrate the effectiveness of using traditional deep learning models on large, unlabeled music datasets for playlist recommendation. Specifically, we utilize CNNs to analyze audio features extracted from large datasets of song ratings and demonstrate the ability to recognize genres and reconstruct low-dimensional embeddings of unlabeled music data. The accuracy of these embeddings is comparable to those obtained using labeled data, and they are useful for playlist recommendation tasks.

A novel linearized stochastic hydrodynamic scheme has been developed to simulate non-equilibrium quantum correlations in mesoscopic semiconductor systems, and proof of its effectiveness was demonstrated through the simulation of the quantum von Neumann entropy density in a quantum dot. This new method was found to accurately capture the onset of oscillations in quantum correlations out of equilibrium, achieving this result by introducing a specific rescaling of the hydrodynamic equations which directly matches the Compton wavelength of the charge, and also ensuring that the quantum entropy entropy density follows the same time evolution as the full quantum system.

Current action proposal generation methods primarily focus on individual video frames, neglecting the rich information contained in adjacent frames. To address this limitation, a Dual Context Aggregation Network (DCAN) has been developed to aggregate contextual information across spatial and temporal dimensions. By processing each frame's context as a separate input, DCAN enables the consideration of near neighbor frames as a contextual element for the current frame, and vice versa. Through dual context aggregation modules, DCAN effectively fuses spatial and temporal contextual information, leading to enhanced feature representation. Comprehensive experiments on popular action proposal datasets, including ActivityNet, yield state-of-the-art results, outperforming the current top-ranking method, OR-TensorGroupConv3D, by 2.19 APE in the challenging sub-shot setting. Moreover, DCAN demonstrates superior robustness in response to frame variations.

Edge localized modes (ELMs) and magnetic islands can generate perturbations on plasma edges that lead to the creation of edge localized modes in microwave systems. Observations from the ECRH system on JET indicate a specific frequency and edge location that correlate with ELMs and magnetic islands, leading to a distinct mode category called palm tree modes (PTMs). A scan of all possible beam-launch locations relative to the magnetic island or ELM focus reveals that only a narrow, specific range of locations can produce the PTMs frequency. This frequency is not altered by changes in island size or ELM energy release. A simple ray-tracing model explains the PTMs frequency by showing that the interaction between the electron cyclotron resonance and edge plasma occurs at the same frequency regardless of island size. A mode category called PTMs is proposed, encompassing all modes resulting from the interaction between the electron cyclotron resonance and magnetic islands or ELMs.

To enhance safety in robot motion planning, a new class of potential fields has been introduced that allows robots to avoid each other through a repulsive force directed towards the centroid of a disk centered on the closest point of approach. By assuming that the disk's vorticity is negative, its rotation can be reinterpreted as a force that pushes the other robot away from its own perspective, thus preventing the field from causing the robot to collide with it. In this paper, the mathematical properties of the new field are analyzed, and it is shown that it meets the criteria for monotonic decrease and the gradient theorem, allowing it to be used in motion planning algorithms based on gradient descent. The paper also compares the fields numerically and visually, and discusses their implications for future research.

Consider a renewal process on the space of infinite sequences generated by an independent and identically distributed process, where the renewal process meets certain technical conditions. If its tail exponent is greater than 1, the process is known to have a quenched large deviation principle for individual letter frequencies. However, if its tail exponent is greater than 1 but less than 2, it now has a scaled and centered large deviation principle for all renewal processes on the space of sequences, conditioned on a specific sequence. If its tail exponent is greater than 1 but less than 2, it now has a quenched large deviation principle for all letter frequencies, conditioned on a specific sequence.

In scenarios where the line-of-sight link is weak or obstructed, a key challenge in radar technology is mitigating the effects of multipath propagation. A key to overcoming this limitation is the use of intelligent reflecting surface technology, which enables radar systems to actively control the propagation of signals. This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing the reflection coefficients of an intelligent surface in a dual-hop AF relay radar system. By treating the surface as an active reflector that can modulate the state of polarization, the proposed algorithm significantly improves the received signal power at the radar terminal. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the surface-modulated dual-polarization approach yields a 10 dB gain in received power compared to conventional algorithms. This technique is particularly effective in scenarios with weak line-of-sight links or high levels of background noise.

The quality of software fuzzers is difficult to assess due to the random nature of their testing processes, making it hard to compare them effectively. A crucial factor in evaluating fuzzers is their ability to induce diverse mutations, as this promotes the discovery of a wider range of vulnerabilities. To address this comparison challenge, advanced mutation analysis techniques have been developed to evaluate and compare fuzzers more accurately. These techniques utilize specialized tools to simulate systematic changes in code and detect defects in the software, thereby assessing the effectiveness of each fuzzer under test. The evaluation of these fuzzers is then based on the number of defects induced in various applications and the level of diversity in the generated inputs, ultimately facilitating a more precise comparison of their performance.

Pretrained models excel in various tasks across different domains. Yet, developing a classifier for a new task with only the model's initial information proves challenging. We investigate the efficacy of using nearest mean classifiers, either individually or in an ensemble, for continuous tasks. Our results show that a single nearest mean classifier outperforms most continual learning methods, while an ensemble of models achieves comparable performance to the best continuous learning techniques. Notably, an ensemble of nearest mean classifiers rivals the performance of the best baselines, demonstrating both efficiency and effectiveness.

If a manifold M has a trivial second homotopy group, we can demonstrate that any map f from a manifold N to the product space M\times N that is close to being 1-homotopic is actually 1-homotopic. This finding enhances a previous result from 1991 by Edwards, Lusk, and Watson. Furthermore, we provide a specific example to illustrate that this broader consequence is indeed valid.

The paper investigates the long-term behavior of solutions to a specific partial differential equation under varying conditions. When the equation is coupled with an external force, the study examines an alternative approach and extends existing stability theories to a broader class of equations. Specifically, the research focuses on an integral equation that models a reaction-diffusion process with an external force, and the results can be applied to a similar equation represented by a partial differential equation. The findings demonstrate that in situations where the equilibrium point is either locally or globally asymptotically stable, the solution to the equation will eventually converge to that equilibrium point. The research also highlights the importance of differentiating between local and global stability in the analysis of the equation's solutions.

The 64Ni nucleus, which lies at the center of the N=40 island, has its excitation energies influenced by a subshell gap that is subject to the monopole interaction. By combining the available experimental data on B(M1) values with large-scale shell model calculations, researchers have gained insight into the gap's impact. The study reveals that the M1 transitions in 64Ni are driven by the monopole interaction, which closes the gap, and as a result, the energy of the 0+2 state is lowered, and the 2+1 state also benefits from this effect, although to a lesser degree. The research shows that the energy difference between the 0+1 and 2+1 states in 64Ni is significantly lower than in the 64Zn isotope, which has a larger gap, and this disparity is attributed to the monopole interaction's effect on the energy levels within the closed shell region.

We introduce a broadened version of Lipschitz games, characterized by distinct Lipschitz constants for each player, and prove its equivalence to a specific mean-field game system that incorporates quadratic cost functions and a general mobility rule within a defined reachable set. Additionally, we have demonstrated the connection between this broadened version and a particular type of stochastic differential game, which also utilizes player-specific Lipschitz constants.

Our investigation into the reliability of performance metrics obtained through model selection and training is confirmed by theoretical and empirical evidence, which shows that jk-fold cross validation provides more stable estimates than standard k-fold cross validation. Specifically, our findings indicate that jk-fold cross validation yields performance metrics with smaller standard errors compared to standard k-fold cross validation, especially when working with limited training data. We derive the error variance of the mean squared error of the performance metric and demonstrate that it is minimized when the number of folds equals twice the square root of the training sample size, thus justifying the use of jk-fold cross validation. Our study also offers practical guidance for statisticians and data analysts to choose the optimal number of folds for cross validation validation based on the size of their training dataset.

Recent advances in neural network architectures have made the Teacher-Student method a prominent learning technique, enabling the efficient training of lightweight student networks with high performance. However, the risk of the student becoming entrapped in local minima due to the absence of the teacher's guidance has become a significant concern. To address this issue, a novel robust Teacher-Student approach is introduced, leveraging the benefits of adversarial training to enhance the student's performance. In this method, the trained student network demonstrates superior performance, outperforming the deep teacher network in various image classification tasks. Specifically, the student network achieves a high accuracy rate of 94.75% on CIFAR-10 with a significantly reduced parameter count of 0.08 million, surpassing the accuracy of the teacher network with 1.04 million parameters.

Bucket Elimination (BE) is a highly efficient algorithm for the comprehensive set of problems known as cost-separation problems. Despite its effectiveness, the complex variable elimination step representing the main bottleneck limits the availability of methods to simplify BE's intricate input data. To circumvent this issue, a new approach called Progressive BE (PBE) is introduced, allowing the elimination step to be broken down into more manageable sub-problems after the initial decomposition of the input data. By applying PBE to BE, the underlying structure can be more easily understood, making it an ideal approach for educational purposes, such as illustrating BE's underlying principles through simple examples.

We've derived an exact expression for the lineshape resulting from strong, unsaturated absorption of a single mode of light, taking into account the effects of photon recoil. The shape is determined by a combination of Rabi frequencies and a saturation parameter, and can be interpreted in terms of these components. Taking a more general view, we've identified various special cases, including the effects of photon recoil in highly saturated situations, multiple component absorption, and absorption of a single mode of light due to multiple processes.

We investigate the jamming transitions in frictionless and frictional isotropic packings under uniform and non-uniform stresses, respectively, and determine the corresponding exponents for various critical phenomena parameters. Our findings indicate that frictionless isotropic jamming and frictional shear jamming exhibit distinct critical exponents, contradicting earlier suggestions of equivalence between these two jamming states. Specifically, the exponents $T^{2
u}$, $K_{B}^{1/	heta}$, $K_{B}^{1/\kappa}$, and $K_{B}^{1/	au}$ differ between them, with values $
u=0.44$, $	heta=0.16$, $\kappa=0.5$, and $	au=0.5$ for frictionless isotropic jamming, and $
u=0.45$, $	heta=0.18$, $\kappa=0.5$, and $	au=0.5$ for frictional shear jamming. Notably, the exponent $
u$ distinguishes these two jamming states, with a ratio of $
u_{shear}/
u_{isotropic}\approx 1.023$.

Researchers are examining the properties of programs that generate Hilbert-Poincar\'e series for specific algebraic structures. Notably, they are analyzing the expression and behavior of the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series for the centralizer $Z(n)(s\ell_2)$ and its relationship with the $n$-th cyclotomic structure $\mathbb{C}(\zeta_n)$ and the field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$. By utilizing a novel approach to the properties of cyclotomic structures, they are able to derive a formula for the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series of $Z(n)(s\ell_2)$ and demonstrate that its specialization corresponds to the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series of the $n$-th cyclotomic structure $\mathbb{C}(\zeta_n)$, thereby resolving a long-standing conjecture. Additionally, they are able to leverage this breakthrough to establish a connection between the algebraic structure $Z(n)(s\ell_2)$ and the field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ for all $n$.

A new type of magnetic multilayer, composed of two adjacent layers with different spin interactions, has been theoretically modeled using a 2D tight-binding method. This structure involves two parallel layers of different spin orientations, where one layer has a strong on-site energy difference and the other has a significant nearest-neighbor interaction, allowing these interactions to be controlled independently. Our calculations demonstrate that the DM interactions' strength can be independently adjusted in comparison to these on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions. A specific relationship between the energy and spin orientation was established and utilized to determine the total magnetic energy in each layer. The resulting total magnetic energy spectrum was analyzed to identify the applicable conditions for quantum magnetism in the two layers. The requirements for interlayer coupling to dominate over other interactions were established, and we identified the possible scenarios for both layers being driven towards quantum magnetism simultaneously. The necessary conditions for both layers being driven towards quantum magnetism simultaneously have been established, and the possible scenarios for both layers being driven towards quantum magnetism simultaneously have been identified.

The number of Standard Model WIMPs that can be detected depends significantly on the velocity distribution of these particles as they interact with our galaxy. Researchers have previously studied the one-dimensional velocity distribution of WIMPs as they approach Earth, but they have also shown that this one-dimensional view is not representative of the entire velocity distribution of approaching WIMPs. In their analysis, they have quantified the probability of detecting a specific one-dimensional velocity distribution of WIMPs, and found that this probability peaks at an approximate velocity of 500 km/s. Furthermore, they have found that the most probable one-dimensional velocity distribution of WIMPs does not match their overall velocity distribution, and that the most probable one-dimensional distribution is actually a "tail" of the most probable two-dimensional velocity distribution. In their analysis, they have also considered the impact of the cut-off of the WIMP velocity distribution, and found that this cut-off has a significant effect on the probability of detecting a specific one-dimensional velocity distribution of WIMPs.

Public sector professionals frequently rely on Web search engines for information, but they often use generic browser defaults without considering the algorithms that shape search results. This study investigates algorithmic prejudices in search engines' top-ranked results for common public sector searches. A comprehensive evaluation framework was developed to assess bias risks in four dimensions: legal, ethical, social, and factual. The researchers examined 1500 search results for twenty diverse public sector-related queries, using both Google and Bing. The study discovered a significant prevalence of algorithmic prejudices in both search engines, with biases affecting various aspects of search results. Furthermore, the analysis revealed notable differences between Google's and Bing's algorithms, as well as variations in the types of biases found for different searches. The research highlights the importance of raising public sector professionals' algorithmic awareness and suggests that organizations should prioritize transparent search engine policies to mitigate bias risks.

A 1-10 TeV, 1-10 TeV, or 10-30 TeV TeV-scale muon collider complex has the potential to explore beyond the Standard Model (BSM) through various particle production processes.  Utilizing the design specifications of the Mμ = 1 TeV,  N=10^32 (CLIC-like) and  N=10^34 (ILC-like) cases,  this study assesses how different BSM scenarios could be assessed based on their cross-sectional area,  energy scale,  and whether they involve new long-lived particles,  new resonances,  new scalar particles,  new vector bosons,  or new types of interactions.  Additionally,  it finds that a 1-10 TeV muon collider can effectively distinguish between the Higgs doublet and bulk supersymmetry,  while a 10-30 TeV muon collider is capable of distinguishing between the Higgs doublet,  bulk supersymmetry,  and direct gauge vector boson generation.  Furthermore,  it finds that a 1-10 TeV muon collider can effectively distinguish between the Higgs doublet and bulk supersymmetry,  while a 10-30 TeV muon collider is capable of distinguishing between the Higgs doublet,  bulk supersymmetry,  and direct gauge vector boson generation.  It also finds that a 1-10 TeV muon

We introduce rCASPR sampling, a novel approach that builds upon traditional linear sampling methods by utilizing a reference PSF obtained through approximate iterative algorithms. This reference PSF serves as a starting point to correct distortions in sampled data, resulting in improved PSF and image contrast compared to conventional methods. Through numerical simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of rCASPR sampling by applying the method to traditional linear sampling and comparing the outcomes to exact values. Furthermore, an analysis of the relationship between rCASPR sampling parameters and its performance is provided, revealing that the method excels particularly in situations with high anisotropic spreading.

Integrating multiple tasks with conflicting objectives represents a common challenge in control design. Recent advancements in Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) have provided a framework for managing systems with conflicting specifications. This study introduces a novel concept, ICCBFs, which generalizes CBFs to accommodate a broader class of systems characterized by Higher Order Control Barrier Functions (HOCBFs). Building on the HOCBF foundation, ICCBFs can handle multiple governing rules, enabling the determination of a feasible control solution. This approach is particularly useful for systems governed by hybrid logic rules. This research is complemented by a control design method for discrete-time continuous-state systems. Moreover, the safety of the proposed algorithm has been verified through the confirmation of closed-loop system ultimate boundedness. Ultimately, this work is accompanied by an example application, involving a vehicle navigating through an obstacle-laden environment.

Continuous domains form the basis for a variety of applications in logic-based programming, reasoning, and verification. Research on continuous domains has expanded to include domains with continuous closure properties, or CF-domains, and their approximations, or CF-spaces. These domains provide precise answers for queries about sets with specific properties. This paper delves deeper into the properties of these domains, presenting a comprehensive analysis of sets with certain closure properties within approximations of continuous domains, or CF-closed sets. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates the relationship between these sets and continuous domains, or C-domains. This relationship is further utilized to enhance domain operations such as fixpoint iteration and continuous functions. The paper also introduces a new class of sets, or pre-CF-closed sets, providing a more accurate description of sets with certain closure properties within approximations of continuous domains, or pre-CF-spaces. These sets are a more general case of CF-closed sets, or C-domains.

Chen and Liu introduced a new exact algorithm for the paired-permutation test, which has a nearly identical efficiency to Monte Carlo approximations. Specifically, the exact algorithm has an average-case time complexity of approximately 0.16 seconds per 10^-9 level of precision on a modern computer, making it nearly indistinguishable from the 0.14 seconds required for a Monte Carlo approximation at the same precision level. This significant advancement addresses previous criticisms of the paired-permutation test and enables its reliable use in practice.

This paper examines the recent collapse of shipping cartels in the global shipping market. Our analysis suggests that a small group of powerful shipping companies dominated the market through illegal price-fixing agreements from 2005 to 2019, effectively controlling freight rates and shipping quantities. Our research reveals that the shipping cartel broke down in 2020 due to an increase in new shipbuilding, entry of smaller carriers, and changes in market practices. We model this transition and find that the collapse of the cartel resulted in increased freight rates and shipping quantities, although the effects were delayed until 2021-2022, with a peak in 2022, and were influenced by external events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russian-Ukrainian conflict.

Loom theory combines elements from the study of looms and the topology of simplicial complexes. A loom model is represented by a system of strings that intersect and cross one another, resulting in a pattern of simplical intersections. By associating this pattern with a specific type of triangulation called a loom space, researchers are able to study topological properties and patterns. All loom spaces can be categorized into two types: beta-looms and gamma-looms, with specific properties and relationships to other topological structures. Loom theory also provides tools for analyzing and constructing complex structures, and has connections to other areas of mathematics and computer science. By defining a loom as a specific type of space that arises from a loom model, researchers are able to apply topological methods to analyze looms and their associated structures, and are able to use these structures to model and analyze other complex systems.

In the field of graph neural networks, a key question remains: How do graph structures and node features interact to impact network classification accuracy? Current GNNs primarily focus on learning node representations, while the structural information within graphs is learned less effectively due to the propagation aggression issue. Our analysis indicates that aggressive propagation leads to the mixing of distinct graph classes due to the exposure of sensitive node information. To address this concern, we introduce a new paradigm, StructGraph, that limits propagation based on graph connectivity, thereby enhancing classification performance. Our experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional GNNs, with a notable improvement of up to 85% in accuracy for certain tasks, while our method exhibits comparable efficiency to standard GNNs.

A dimensionality reduction method called non-parametric adaptive dimensionality reduction (NA-AdAR) addresses the limitations of traditional techniques by introducing an adaptive input that withstands various forms of corruption, including malicious data, for example, those produced by an adversary manipulating the input to mislead the algorithm. Unlike other methods, NA-AdAR's performance is not significantly impaired when using real data that deviates from the expected distribution in comparison to traditional methods. We prove the accuracy of NA-AdAR's reduced representations to be comparable to those of the underlying real data, even when the data distribution is unknown. We demonstrate the efficacy of NA-AdAR through experiments utilizing both synthetic and real-world data, showcasing its adaptability in the presence of real-world data variations and its resistance to adversarial data. The code is available online for replication of the results.

In our previous work, we demonstrated that compact submanifolds with singularities in a class that includes those generated by minimal surfaces under conformal deformations, exhibit specific geometric properties when their dimension satisfies certain conditions. Specifically, we found that in dimensions 2k+1, these submanifolds consist of disconnected surfaces connected by surfaces with F-stacks in dimensions k. Our main theorem expands on this finding by demonstrating that in dimensions 2k, these submanifolds comprise connected surfaces with intersecting points in dimensions k-1. Our proof involves a surgery-style argument, which enables the removal of singularities with certain dimensions, allowing us to reduce the study of these submanifolds to previously understood cases. Our results also demonstrate that 1-dimensional singularities on compact submanifolds with certain dimension and dimension properties are always discrete.

A new theory to understand the behavior of vortex cores in superconductors has been developed, indicating that moving magnetic flux lines possess significant entropy. This entropy is comparable to that of quasiparticle pairs in the vortex core. In contrast, the entropy of the moving flux line dominates the entropy of the superconducting gap in the momentum space. This distinction highlights the limitations of previous models that equate the entropy of moving flux lines and vortex cores. A key finding of this new framework reveals that the entropy of moving flux lines is proportional to the superconducting gap in the momentum space, ultimately leading to a saturation of entropy as the gap closes. This theoretical approach is further supported by experimental data, demonstrating an increase in entropy across all materials examined.

A new method called maximum entropy feedback (MEF) was investigated for its effectiveness in enabling an efficient and optimal coordination between an aggregator and the system operator in a scenario involving decentralized energy management. Initially, theoretical proofs showed that MEF leads to an equilibrium that benefits all parties and makes it possible to achieve an optimal solution through iterative optimization. To test MEF in real-world applications, a simulation was developed to mimic real-time transactions between the aggregator and multiple systems. Results from these simulations confirmed that MEF can handle a high volume of transactions and efficiently manage decentralized energy management.

Our research takes a comprehensive approach to enhancing stock prediction capabilities. We created a series of features that incorporate technical indicators and historical price data, allowing a conventional machine learning model to accurately forecast future prices. In particular, our analysis leverages the Scikit-Finance library to develop these features, thereby demonstrating their effectiveness in robust price forecasting.

A rare category of supernovae, which comprise less than one percent of all such events, is thought to be caused by the merger of two compact stars, specifically where one of the components is a white dwarf. Researchers propose that these events are more frequent than previously estimated, occurring roughly 26 times per year, with half of them producing a bright optical transient. Simulations indicate that these explosions would emit electromagnetic radiation across the spectrum, making them detectable even if they occur in distant galaxies. A study of existing data from the LIGO Laboratory and a systematic survey of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, the Palomar Transient Fusion Survey Project, and the Catalina Sky Survey for potential counterparts, has not revealed any instances of this type of supernova. However, simulations suggest that future observations with the Square Kilometre Array and the James Webb Space Telescope for electromagnetic signals from white dwarf mergers, could yield up to 10 detections within the next 10 years.

We have derived the Leading Power Counting Higgs Effective Field Theory at next-to-next-to-leading order in terms of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory when considering double Higgs production in deep inline collisions. The results allow for the identification of certain Standard Model effective operators which contribute significantly to this process, specifically C_2, C_3, C_5, C_6, O_1, O_2, O_3, O_4, O_5, O_6, O_7, O_8, O_9, O_{10}, O_{11}, O_{12}, O_{13}, O_{14}, O_{15}, O_{16}, O_{17}, O_{18}, O_{19}, O_{20}, O_{21}, O_{22}, O_{23}, O_{24}, O_{25}, O_{26}, O_{27}, O_{28}, O_{29}, O_{30}, O_{31}, O_{32}, O_{33}, O_{34}, O_{35}, O_{36}, O_{37}, O_{38}, O_{39}, O_{40}, O_{41}, O_{42}, O_{43}, O_{44}, O_{45}, O_{46}, O_{47}, O_{48}, O_{49}, O_{50}, O_{51}, O_{52}, O_{53}, O_{54}, O_{55}, O_{56},

We utilize an early expression for non-relativistic metrics, which facilitates analytical expansions, and apply it to derive an approximate analytical formula for the ADM mass in asymptotically flat spacetimes within general relativity.

By breaking down the Einstein equations into two distinct sets of differential equations, we have developed an alternative computational approach to determining boundary observables in General Relativity. This new method involves solving a reduced set of algebraic equations derived from the decoupled equations of motion to determine the boundary values of massless fields, which can be used to compute observable quantities at the boundary. Utilizing this approach, we have developed a computer assistant capable of executing these calculations for a specific class of solutions representing $n$-dimensional black branes located within a $d$-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetime.

We investigated the drag experienced by a cylindrical solid moving through different types of granular materials under varying driving forces, observing a complex relationship that depends on the force and accelerates from laminar to turbulent behavior. Notably, the drag increased with the square of the driving rate when the intruder accelerates at a rate equal to the gravitational acceleration, and we discovered a critical angle of around 5-7 degrees for frictionless grains that minimizes the drag and corresponds to a stable position of the intruder. Changing the driving force also caused changes in the granular bed, resulting in hysteresis effects that influenced the drag and allowed the bed to store energy that is released when the driving force is reduced.

Using data from KCWI and HST, we studied the ionized gas outflows in seven starbursting disk galaxies with low interstellar medium reserves using custom analysis techniques. Our observations revealed the presence of mass-loss rates comparable to those in galaxies with sustained star formation, with outflows transporting 1-10 $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ of gas from their host galaxies. Notably, we found that these outflows prevent gas depletion, maintaining galaxy disk reserves for 10^8-10^9 years. Outflows account for 10-100 times more gas mass lost than supernova explosions, indicating that supernovae explosions have a minimal impact on mass loss. Our findings suggest that the mass loss caused by supernovae is largely offset by gas reaccumulation, with mass loss ultimately being driven by galaxy-scale processes.

Large-scale experiments involving complex systems, private data, and costly computations often require finding efficient configurations that balance performance, security, and resource utilization. This process is often hindered by the large number of possible configurations, leading to significant costs and waiting times when using traditional methods based on grid search or random sampling. To address this challenge, we introduce BoAnon, an active learning algorithm that efficiently identifies top-performing configurations by selecting sample points to run experiments. By leveraging a surrogate model, BoAnon estimates the expected improvement in performance for each possible configuration and prioritizes the most promising ones. We demonstrate BoAnon's effectiveness in a series of experiments, showing it discovers high-quality configurations in a fraction of the time required by traditional methods. For example, in one experiment, BoAnon found a top-1% configuration within 10% of the total cost, compared to BoAnon taking 90% of the total cost using grid search.

The ALICE experiment at the CERN LHC measured the transverse momentum dependence of triangular flow $v_3$ and elliptic flow $v_2$ for pions, kaons, and protons in lead-lead collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=2.76$ TeV. When comparing $v_3$ and $v_2$, the measured $p_T$ dependence is consistent with a power-law function $p_T^{-\phi}$, with the power $\phi$ equal to $0.92\pm0.06$ based on the combined data analysis of different centrality classes. This power-law dependence holds across a range of $0.3<p_T<10$ GeV/c and is independent of the collision centrality or identified particle type.

Large RDF datasets are frequently utilized in web-scale applications and require efficient high-performance quality assessment methods. Existing quality assessment techniques for RDF are often limited due to their focus on specific aspects, whereas a comprehensive evaluation tool is desperately needed. We introduce DQA, a cutting-edge quality assessment framework for large RDF datasets, which combines advanced techniques including graph partitioning, data sampling, and parallel processing to deliver exceptional performance while providing accurate quality assessments. Unlike conventional methods, DQA employs a novel approach to evaluate RDF data quality, separating quality criteria into two categories: those that require direct assessment and those that benefit from graph structure analysis. By leveraging this distinction, DQA is able to effectively evaluate RDF datasets with high efficiency. The design of DQA's evaluation algorithms ensures accurate results, and our experiments demonstrate its superior performance, achieving up to 10 times faster assessment speeds compared to existing methods.

This study explores the performance of minimum density power divergence (MDPDE) and maximum likelihood (MLE) estimators for various independent increment and Markov processes, including specific examples like Poisson processes, Brownian with a drift, and autoregressive processes. Notably, our research indicates that under specific conditions, MDPDEs are comparable to MLEs and both result in asymptotically efficient estimates. Furthermore, our findings reveal that MDPDEs can be a viable alternative to MLEs, especially when the data follows a process with independent increments. In such cases, MDPDEs produce similar results to MLEs with a key advantage - they do not require the ordering of observations, which is otherwise necessary for MLEs.

The complex interplay between gas and black hole in active galaxies, particularly how shock-ionization influences observable gas properties, is not yet fully understood. To investigate this, we developed a simple two-component model, incorporating a radiative active nucleus surrounded by a vast gas reservoir. Through computations, we analyzed various shock mechanisms, including electron scattering and bremsstrahlung radiation, and their impact on producing specific spectral features. Our findings show that radiative effects can significantly alter shock patterns, resulting in altered distributions of ionization, temperature, and metal abundance. Consequently, shock patterns are transformed, influencing line intensity and profile, ultimately distorting the expected relationships between these observables and radiative energy. Notably, when considering observable relationships, we find that line intensity versus line width can exhibit a linear correlation, consistent with previous research, although this linear relationship may not always hold when considering different gas regions. Furthermore, we find that line intensity can serve as a reliable proxy for gas velocity, temperature, and metal abundance, offering a key insight for future observational and theoretical analyses.

Researchers use the Frisbee framework to create and run tests on IoT applications, but its potential limitations in simulation-based testing remain unclear. Frisbee's benefits, such as reduced costs and quicker testing, are offset by the need to write complex test code and the risk of simulation inaccuracies. However, the study shows that Frisbee can effectively identify bugs causing crashes and memory leaks, and even detect latent issues in some cases, and and suggest ways to improve its performance. The research reveals that the most common issue found through Frisbee testing is related to synchronization primitives, and it works best for finding crashes and memory leaks, but less reliable for finding other types of bugs. The study also shows that the number of bugs found decreases as the size of the test program increases, and it's more efficient at finding bugs in programs that use multiple threads. The authors propose several ways to improve the performance of the tool, such as using static analysis to identify potential issues before running the test program, and they suggest that the tool could be more reliable at finding certain types of bugs, like those related to data types, through further research and development.

New limits on the rare occurrences of B meson decay are established by the LHCb collaboration. When subjected to the full range of their respective datasets, the rare happenings of B^0_s to mu+ mu- and B^0 to mu+ mu- fail to occur at frequencies below 8.4 x 10^-11 and 2.6 x 10^-10, respectively. Moreover, a more precise limit on the occurrence of B^0_s to mu+ mu- below 2.1 x 10^-10 has been established than previously reported.

Generating realistic and comprehensive 3D traffic scenes for training self-driving vehicles is a challenging task due to the complexity of road environments. Current approaches often rely on manual scene editing or use limited sets of rules to generate scenes. In response to these limitations, we've developed SceneGen, a novel framework that combines symbolic representations and 3D rendering techniques to create detailed and photorealistic traffic scenes. In contrast to existing methods, SceneGen treats scene generation as a problem of rendering symbolic data rather than a rule-based system. By doing so, it enhances the expressiveness of scene descriptions and allows for more efficient updates of scene components. We've tested SceneGen by generating over 10,000 scenes and comparing them to real-world scenes, showing that they are not only visually similar but also accurately capture the semantic information present in real scenes. In terms of performance, SceneGen outperforms existing methods by creating scenes with more than double the number of objects and achieves a level of realism that matches that of real scenes as judged by human assessors.

Consider a Cayley tree structured according to a given group representation, to which we apply the Potts model at its pure free boundary conditions. By using the method of partial sums, we derive explicit formulas for the two-point function, magnetization, and correlation between distinct Potts components. Furthermore, we investigate the convergence of the Gibbs distribution with respect to the topology of the Cayley tree, demonstrating that it converges to a non-translation-invariant Gibbs distribution on the d-dimensional lattice when the degree of the tree approaches infinity, provided that the group representation has no element of order two and is finite.

This research introduces an innovative, high-performance variant of the Generalized Minimum Residual Method (GMRES) called the Preconditioned Flexible Generalized Minimum Residual Method (PFGMRES) for solving systems of linear equations. The PFGMRES method was initially developed to accommodate an exceptional degree of flexibility in the choice of iteration parameters, allowing it to achieve precise control over the residual vectors within the Krylov subspace. As a result, this method is capable of producing outstanding numerical solutions, particularly in situations where the initial guess has a significant impact on the solution. To further enhance its performance, the PFGMRES method incorporates a novel orthogonalization technique based on the level of precision specified, which is designed to minimize the generation of unnecessary information during the iteration process. To evaluate the efficiency of the PFGMRES method, several numerical experiments were conducted using various sample problems, demonstrating its superiority over the standard GMRES method in terms of iteration count, orthogonalization step count, and total floating point operations.

Induced expansions and joint ergodicity have been proven for a specific trio of potentials p(q(x))x^2, p(x^2) and p(x^3) where p is a non-degenerate parabola, under the condition that p has a positive leading coefficient. This condition is crucial as it makes the potential non-degenerate. If the coefficient is zero for one of the potentials, the problem becomes less clear-cut. For instance, consider the potential p(q(x))x^2, which is often associated with the Sturm-Liouville problem and has been extensively studied, especially when p is the Laplacian operator. Despite its widespread occurrence, there is a significant gap in knowledge regarding joint ergodicity for this particular case of the Sturm-Liouville problem. Our work builds upon a recent publication by Hai Qian, Xing Qian and Zhiyuan Wang, who obtained a more detailed analysis of the ergodicity constants for the potential p(x^2) on the torus T^d. Our main contribution is an explicit expression of (P_t phi_+, P_s phi_-), as well as its asymptotic behavior as t approaches infinity, for the potential p(q(x))x^2. This expression is a key result in answering a long-standing question posed by H. Qian, X. Qian and Z. Wang.

The formation of massive stars within the Milky Way's largest molecular clouds can create superbubbles that last for millions of years. These superbubbles provide an ideal environment for the formation of dust grains through the expansion of stellar winds and supernova blasts. Researchers have discovered that pair-instability and core-collapse supernovae play a crucial role in dust production, and their findings suggest this process can result in the creation of heavy elements, such as iron, through the fusion of stellar cores. A study published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics utilizes observations from the Spitzer Space Telescope, along with data from other telescopes, to analyze the dust properties within the massive W3/W4/W5 complex. Analyzing multiple wavelengths of light allowed the researchers to measure dust temperatures between 90 to 110 Kelvin, which is consistent with the temperatures found in the clouds' cores. The team's measurements of dust mass, size, and velocity of expansion were used to create theoretical models, which showed that the dust within these clouds is formed through massive star winds and supernovae, resulting in an estimated production rate of iron of 0.05 solar masses per year. The study also revealed that the iron production rate from these processes is significantly higher than previously estimated, and the researchers suggest that similar processes may also occur within other massive star-forming regions.

To enhance 3D object detection on autonomous systems, a novel fusion approach has been developed, combining the effectiveness of RGB and lidar-based methods in early stages.  Initially, two separate detection systems were employed, one solely using lidar data with a range of 100 meters and the other using both lidar and RGB data up to 50.5 meters.  These systems were then integrated through the merging of their feature maps, allowing for improved performance in far-field object detection.  By optimizing the fusion stage for 3D object detection, a method was developed to adaptively weight the contributions of each detection branch based on their distance from the LiDAR sensor.  This led to a significant improvement of 4.3% in average precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5 when fusing lidar and RGB features, and a notable improvement of 10.2% in far-field conditions (beyond 40 meters).  The code for this research has been made publicly available on the GitHub repository.

A new approach to using quantum machine learning in chemistry has been developed, where a neural network trained on classical data helps prepare complex quantum states quickly. This was demonstrated on a well-studied molecule, formamide, by building a conditional quantum circuit that replicates an energy state simply by inputting the molecular structure. By fine-tuning the neural network with classical data, it learned to mimic the pattern of energy variations across different molecular configurations. Using this approach, researchers were able to efficiently create new quantum states and calculate their energies, even when full quantum simulations became impractically expensive.

Accurate tracking of surgical interventions relies on registering preoperative 3D organ models to actual intraoperative situations. This process, known as image-guided surgery, can be complicated by unpredictable movements and the natural flexibility of tissues during operations. Additionally, the presence of surgical tools can hinder visibility and make it difficult to obtain clear images. Existing methods for estimating the organ's shape from surgical video footage have limitations when it comes to handling noise-prone data, which is common during operations. To address these challenges, we've developed a novel approach that uses a deep learning tool to analyze data from the surgical operating room, even when the data is noisy and difficult to interpret. By leveraging the strengths of convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks, our method effectively handles uncertain and flexible organ movements, outperforming current techniques according to our evaluation results.

The concept of conformal matter collineations is examined for degenerate energy-momentum tensors, determining the number of collineation degrees of freedom in this scenario to be infinite-dimensional.

Estimating optical flow in self-supervised learning has made significant progress in recent years, however, several challenges still persist, notably the issue of occlusions which have a persistent impact on both natural and synthetic datasets. To mitigate this effect, the majority of learning-based approaches tend to rely heavily on the assumption of smoothness and brightness consistency across boundaries. In contrast to these approaches, predicting correspondence by assuming continuity across the occluder rather than the boundary itself offers a more promising alternative. To tackle this, we introduce a novel self-supervised loss function, based on a consistency constraint along a straight line, to estimate optical flow, particularly effective in addressing occlusions. Notably, this approach demands minimal assumptions about light and smoothness, and can be seamlessly integrated with existing self-supervised methods. Comprehensive experimental results on seven public datasets demonstrate the enhanced performance of our method, especially in scenarios with significant occlusions, outperforming the current state-of-the-art by a considerable margin of up to 10% in terms of EPE.

Deep learning techniques have significantly transformed the classification domain, however, neural networks often require massive data sets for training and have high power consumption rates. To address these limitations, we introduce a general-purpose classifier based on the spiking neural network model, known as the Eilon-Like weight update rule (ELW). In comparison to ANNs, ELW exhibits comparable performance while significantly reducing power consumption. In our research, we present an in-depth analysis of the ELW model, followed by experimental results utilizing MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 data sets, demonstrating its effectiveness.

Researchers investigated the effects of a strong magnetic field on the behavior of spin-polarized quark matter under extreme conditions, particularly for temperatures and densities found in neutron stars. They developed a Gleich-Ebert model that incorporates the influence of a magnetic field on the masses of quarks and calculated how it impacts the quark matter's equation of state. The results showed that the magnetic field has a significant impact on the spin-polarized quark matter's behavior, potentially leading to its magnetization and causing the onset of a degenerate state known as the "crystal state" to be delayed in neutron stars. The research also revealed that a strong magnetic field can increase the minimum density required for quark stars to exist and that their minimum mass is highly sensitive to the magnetic field's strength. However, the findings suggest that the magnetic field's impact may be mitigated by the presence of electrons, which could result in a smaller minimum mass required for quark stars. The study further found that the magnetic field's influence on the star's crust could cause it to contract and spin faster, consistent with the observed properties of the neutron star XTE J1710-273.

A cubic graph is classified as even-2-factorable (E2F) if it has a 2-factor consisting of two disjoint components with even degrees. The 2-factorability problem for cubic graphs was initially proven possible by showing that an E2F graph must have a 2-factor meeting specific criteria. As a result, determining if a cubic graph is even-2-factorable is equivalent to determining the existence of a 2-factor that meets those criteria. To resolve this problem, a new algorithm was developed that can identify whether a cubic graph is even-2factorable. The algorithm is based on the concept of searching for a specific type of star forest within the graph's neighborhood sequence set. The determination of the adequacy of a star forest is made possible by creating a new evaluation function that compares the degrees of the stars within the forest to the degrees of the graph's original vertices. The development of this algorithm represents a significant advancement in the study of even-2factorable cubic graphs, as it provides a clear method for determining this property for any given graph. The algorithm's efficiency is comparable to other known algorithms for determining similar graph properties, as it operates with a time complexity of O(n^2).

Li has analytically examined a modified version of the Bateman-Horn Conjecture, yielding a more precise prime estimation for a specific family of quadratic polynomials, $A(x^2+1)+B(x^2-1)+C(x^2-x)+D$, where $A, B, C, D$ are integers, with a conjectured frequency of $O(x^4)$ for prime values within the range $[x, 2x]$. Building upon the work of Pomerance and Young, Li's findings refine earlier results by Bourdon, Friedlander, Pomerance, and Young, who found a similar family of quadratic polynomials with a prime value frequency of $O(x^4)$ but with a different structure.

To efficiently protect services from malicious user data, a technique called filter-then-execution has been an effective method for reducing the impact of attacks. However, this approach is often limited to compiled applications and system calls. We present Timeloops, an innovative system that extends the benefits of technique-based protection to applications written in interpreted languages, such as Python, Ruby, and PHP, even when they utilize system calls. We demonstrate a prototype implementation of a module for the SQLite database management system and several popular web applications, revealing that our system achieves substantial reductions in latency and enhanced security. Furthermore, our system remains compatible with the existing application code.

Dark matter, comprised of a pseudo-Goldstone boson, can only interact with nucleons through weak interactions mediated by light vectors or Higgs-like particles. These interactions result in dark matter's elastic scattering being influenced by its mass and the masses of the underlying Goldstone and nucleon. As a consequence, the standard treatment of dark matter scattering, which assumes a strong interaction with nucleons, is no longer applicable. Instead, the dark matter's pseudo-Goldstone nature leads to scattering cross-sections that are highly variable and often exceed the experimental limits in certain cases. Furthermore, the elastic scattering process is sensitive to the dark matter's velocity, which can result in cross-section fluctuations of up to five orders of magnitude due to its dependence on the nucleon's form factor. As a result, the pseudo-Goldstone boson dark matter scenario can be scrutinized by experimental searches for dark matter using elastic scattering data, which can provide a complementary testing ground for this type of dark matter model.

To tackle the complex problem of tracking unidentified targets with restricted sensor visibility, a new approach has been developed to efficiently update their states over time. By utilizing a dynamic wind sensor model, the possible locations of these targets can be limited, reducing the need to monitor the entire horizon for detections. When a detection occurs, a specialized filter is applied to provide initial assessment, rather than relying on the Kalman filter for all situations. This two-tier approach enhances performance while minimizing computational demands for frequent undetected periods. Comprehensive simulations validate the effectiveness of this method, and it is discovered that the proposed technique surpasses existing methods in terms of target state estimation accuracy, outperforming them by a margin of up to 300 meters in optimal conditions and 1300 meters in suboptimal conditions.

This research paper examines a recent publication by J. Guo and J. Wang, which investigated the dynamics of a population model subject to pollution, observed in J. Wang's 2020 paper. However, the model presented in J. Wang's 2020 paper is incorrect, leading to unbounded solutions. The correct model is presented, and a new approach to proving the observability inequality is found, resulting in the extinction of the population. The model is a system of two equations, representing the interactions between two species, and is defined by the following differential equations: $y_t+\Delta y+\beta y dy=\beta y_0 dy$. The model is modified to eliminate unbounded solutions, and the modified model exhibits the same dynamic behavior as the original model, despite the error. The correct model can be managed through an observability inequality, and this concept is applied to the original model to show that an initial condition is relatively compact in the norm $L^2$, ultimately leading to the extinction of the population. The relationship between the population model and a control system is established, and this connection is used to prove the relative compactness of an initial condition in the norm $L^2$, resulting in the extinction of the population.

Evaluating intelligent decision-making in sports like soccer requires a deep understanding of the game's rules and dynamics. Current approaches to task reinforcement learning overlook the complexities of implementing actions that adhere to game rules, leading to a lack of applicable solutions. To address this, we propose a novel framework called Task Embedding Action Language (TEAL), which allows learners to receive task instructions encoded with actions' meanings and legal application contexts. By testing TEAL on the game of keepaway in 2D, we show that learning agents successfully prioritize high-reward actions like shooting for goal over less valuable actions like committing fouls or sending the ball out of bounds, thus demonstrating the effectiveness of the framework in soccer.

Full waveform inversion (FWI) holds great promise for creating highly accurate velocity models for seismic imaging. However, the time-domain approach to FWI is hindered by the requirement to compute adjoint fields, which is a computationally intensive task. To overcome this limitation, a new method for time-domain wavefield reconstruction has been developed, using a linearized boundary formulation and a reduced-order model to approximate the adjoint wavefield. By reconstructing the time-domain wavefield and using it to compute the residual, we demonstrate significant improvements in convergence rates in synthetic data inversion tests. The method proves particularly effective for large-scale models and long observation time windows. The implementation of this new time-domain reconstruction method is achieved through a combination of Python tools, including the use of the PyGSEIS software for time-domain preconditioning and the FEniCS platform for finite-element discretization.

Photonic systems that use light to control other light transmissions can be complex to assemble using traditional techniques due to difficulties in creating devices that couple light in different ways. To address this challenge, researchers have found success with chiral interresonator coupling, which uses different transmission fidelities to control the transmission of light. By incorporating this method, devices such as all-optical diodes and quasi-circulators can be created without the need for precise control over light direction. A new approach uses metamaterials to achieve similar results, which can be designed more freely due to their ability to control light through volume and surface interactions. By combining two types of coupling, one focused on volume and the other on surface interactions, researchers have demonstrated functional all-optical diodes and quasi-circulators. Furthermore, the ability to design these systems freely has enabled the creation of a multi-directional switch, which can direct light to any of four different channels.

We performed a thorough examination of the 2019 high-energy outburst from IGR J19294+1816* using data from numerous X-ray telescopes. Our joint spectral and temporal analysis across three energy bands revealed the presence of radio and infrared emission corresponding to frequencies of 18.3 GHz, 335.1 microJy, IR band, and an infrared flux of 2.5 x 10^-12 erg cm^-2 s^-1. Notably, we discovered that IGR J19294+1816 exhibited a power-law spectrum with a spectral index of -0.56 over the X-ray range, in contrast to its initial detection in 2008, when its spectrum was described as thermal. Based on its 2019 optical counterpart, we determined the system's orbital period to be approximately 9.62 hours, which is significantly shorter than its previous estimated upper limit.

This study examines an asymmetric noisy voter model, applied to a square lattice with a specific distortion, where individuals are located at the vertices and connected by directed edges representing the influence of others' opinions. The distortion disrupts the equal balance of influence, causing some individuals to be affected more by their connections. The model also incorporates random changes to opinions. The asymmetric property leads to diverse outcomes based on specific distortion and noise levels. The model enters a phase where both species coexist, or results in the dominance of one species over the other, or the opinions become randomly disordered. The model was simulated and analyzed to determine the conditions that lead to these outcomes. The effects of noise and distortion on the model's results were also analyzed. The model shows hysteresis in some cases, where the path to a particular state differs from the path to the same state. The model also exhibits different behavior when starting from different initial conditions. The size of the lattice does not significantly impact the model's results. The model's behavior is also affected by the speed at which opinions change. The study also found that the model exhibits coexistence, monoculture, and chaos phases. The boundaries that separate these phases are non-trivial and unique. The model's behavior was compared to other similar models to identify its distinct characteristics. The model's results were verified through multiple simulations and methods. The study also analyzed the model's behavior over time, showing that the model reaches a stable state within a certain number of steps.

Indonesia, being a vast and populous country with diverse cultures and regions, has significant historical potential waiting to be uncovered. Sundials, as ancient time-telling instruments, offer a unique window into local customs and past lifestyles. Unfortunately, little scientific research has focused on sundials within Indonesia to date. To bridge this knowledge gap, we have developed a web-based platform where citizens can contribute their knowledge and observations about sundials found across the country. Through this platform, users can report and share information about sundials, including their location, photos, and descriptions, which can be further analyzed to extract spatial and temporal data. By gathering this information, we aim to study sundials from a spatial, cultural, and temporal perspective, which can provide valuable insights into local customs and the history of time-telling practices within Indonesia.

In DED2D systems, combining data and energy sharing can enhance efficiency and user satisfaction. A novel slotted TFIET scheme is proposed, separating each time slot into data transmission, energy transfer to users, and idle periods. Two key objectives are optimized: minimizing the average completion time for generating desired data and meeting energy demands, and maximizing user satisfaction. Satisfiability problems result from treating user satisfaction as constraints, so an integer linear program is formulated to solve these problems. Due to computational complexity, a heuristic algorithm is developed for practical slotted TFIET system implementations. Analytical and simulated results for the proposed scheme and its heuristic variant are presented, outperforming existing methods.

The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the shift to remote work, causing a surge in demands for automated, self-sustaining experimental setups in scientific research. Prior to the pandemic, these applications were largely in the early stages of development, with limited deployment due to the complexity of creating robust automation systems. In response to the crisis, researchers were compelled to prioritize the development of automated solutions, leading to a surge in related publications. This surge in interest resulted in the emergence of novel approaches to designing and executing experiments, with researchers leveraging advancements in machine learning, cloud computing, and containerization to create high-performance, efficient, and reliable solutions. As a result of the significant advancements made possible by these innovations, the field of experimental automation has entered a new era of cloud-scale experimentation.

The size and density of an electron probe are critical factors in electron microscopy, influencing the resolution and imaging speed. In electron optical systems that use a scanning probe, the probe size and density are determined by the design of the electrostatic phase plates, which dictate the electron beam's initial characteristics and final shape after focusing. This study investigates the relationship between phase plate design and electron probe properties, which are also affected by other factors such as the fill-factor, pixel pattern, arrangement, and alignment. By conducting simulations and experimental measurements using a hexagonal close-packed design, we found that the probe size and density exhibit an approximate four-fold variation, ranging from 1-4 nm, and 10-40 nA, respectively, depending on the specific design parameters. These findings are explained by the underlying physics governing the electron beam's interaction with the phase plates. It is demonstrated that the optimal design of the phase plates can minimize probe sizes and maximize current densities by creating coherent coherent areas, reducing the formation of artifacts, and optimizing the scattering of electrons. The optimal design also results in improved imaging speeds and resolution in electron microscopy.

Recent advances in dialogue understanding tasks have seen the emergence of RNN-based architectures as a primary choice due to their effective use of contextual information. Despite some RNN-based models' notable achievements, research into the effectiveness of RNNs is still limited. This study compares the performance of RNN-based models, transformer models, and their hybrids in dialogue understanding tasks, revealing that the latter consistently outperforms the former in terms of accuracy, F1-score, and ROUGE score across multiple tasks. Notably, the comparison of RNN-based models and models incorporating the recurrence mechanism shows that removing the recurrence mechanism results in minimal declines in performance, indicating its relatively limited impact. These findings suggest that RNN-based models' primary contributions stem from their utilization of contextual information rather than the recurrence mechanism itself.

To enhance the reliability of mapping algorithms using mobile devices in dynamic and rapidly changing environments, this study proposes an attention-guided loop closure detection method using recurrent and convolutional neural networks. Initially, a baseline model was created by converting a standard 1D grid-based mapping algorithm into a 2D grid-based mapping algorithm. This baseline model was then modified to incorporate an attention mechanism within a deep learning network. By running multiple tests under changing conditions, the research found that the attention-guided approach outperformed the baseline model, achieving a 12% improvement in detection accuracy using a Mobile device and achieving a 5% improvement in detection accuracy using an Intel NUC. Furthermore, the attention-guidance module was found to enhance detection accuracy by an average of 15% in dynamic environments.

The increasing popularity of video streaming over online platforms necessitates a high-quality viewing experience for users, which can be achieved through cloud services maintaining optimal performance. A cloud-based video streaming system was developed, utilizing cloud frontends to deliver continuous Quality of Service (QoS).
